maxPixels.description: Most pixels ONE document may contain — width × height — where that differs from the platform-wide `maxPixels` above, which it REPLACES for this kind rather than narrowing. Null means the platform-wide one applies. Over it is `attachment_too_many_pixels`. LinkedIn is why it sits per kind: its image API refuses anything over 36,152,320 px and its video API publishes no pixel rule at all.

caption.description: Always null. A subtitle file is a kind the media library stores and never a kind a POST carries, so no platform has a rule about how many of them one may hold. Where a subtitle file reaches a platform is a `media` option — see YouTube’s `captionFile` — whose own `mimeTypes` and `maxBytes` are the rules that bind it.

maxCount.description: Most subtitle files one post may carry, where that is tighter than `maxMedia`. Null means only `maxMedia` binds. Over it is `too_many_attachments_of_kind`.

maxBytes.description: Largest ONE subtitle file may be, in bytes. Over it is `attachment_too_large`. The only media rule checked on every attachment — a stored file always has a size, where the duration and dimensions above are measured best-effort and are unknown for every image.

alone.description: True when a subtitle file may not share a post with a file of any other kind. Mixing them is `attachment_kinds_mixed`.

minAspectRatio.description: Lowest width ÷ height accepted for a subtitle file, where that differs from the platform-wide `minAspectRatio` above — it REPLACES that value for this kind rather than narrowing it. Null means the platform-wide one applies. Outside it is `attachment_aspect_unsupported`. Instagram is why: a feed image publishes between 4:5 and 1.91:1 where a video publishes between 0.01:1 and 10:1.

maxAspectRatio.description: Highest width ÷ height accepted for a subtitle file, on the same terms as `minAspectRatio`.

maxPixels.description: Most pixels ONE subtitle file may contain — width × height — where that differs from the platform-wide `maxPixels` above, which it REPLACES for this kind rather than narrowing. Null means the platform-wide one applies. Over it is `attachment_too_many_pixels`. LinkedIn is why it sits per kind: its image API refuses anything over 36,152,320 px and its video API publishes no pixel rule at all.

perType.description: Rules for one exact MIME type, where the kind above is too coarse — `null` on a platform that publishes none, which is most of them. Keyed by the mime type as `media.mimeType` reports it. X is why it exists, and it needs every field: X takes "up to 4 photos, 1 animated GIF, or 1 video", where a GIF and a JPEG are both `image` — so the ceiling (15 MB of animation against 5 MB of still), the count and the exclusion are all facts about a type. `maxBytes` REPLACES the kind's ceiling for this file; `maxCount` is counted alongside the kind's cap rather than replacing it, since five images with one GIF among them are five of the kind and one of the type.

maxBytes.description: Largest ONE file of this exact type may be, in bytes. Over it is `attachment_too_large`, the same error the kind ceiling raises.

maxCount.description: Most files of this exact type one post may carry. Null means only the kind cap and `maxMedia` bind. Over it is `too_many_attachments_of_type`.

alone.description: True when a file of this type may not share a post with a file of any other type — its own kind included, which is what separates it from the per-kind flag. Mixing them is `attachment_types_mixed`.

noun.description: What this platform calls a file of this type in a refusal — "GIF". Null where the kind name is the right word.

remoteEdit.description: What this platform will change about a post that is ALREADY OUT — send it with `POST /public/v1/posts/{id}/revise`. `null` where a published post is final, which includes every platform that offers no update endpoint at all. Only half the answer: whether a GIVEN channel may use it depends on what its connection was granted, which is `manageStatus` on `GET /public/v1/channels`.

fields.description: The parts that change. Attachments are on no platform's list and there is deliberately no member for them: revising cannot change what a post is carrying anywhere. Sending a part that is not listed is `edit_not_supported` — Reddit rewrites a post's body and never its title.

windowMs.description: Milliseconds after publishing during which an edit is still accepted, or `null` for no deadline — which is every platform today. A revision arriving after it is `edit_window_expired`.

supportsRemoteDelete.description: This platform can take a published post back down, so `POST /public/v1/posts/{id}/retract` reaches it. False means a copy published here is permanent as far as this API is concerned — retracting a submission that includes one deletes our record and reports that channel as one whose copy stays up.

Post.description: One submission — a single thing sent to one or more channels. `id` is the submission, not a per-channel row: each channel publishes independently and carries its own status inside `channels`.

id.description: The submission id. Pass this to every `/posts/{id}` route.

status.description: Rolled up across channels. Anything still in flight outranks a mixed terminal state, so a group with one failure and three channels still publishing reports `publishing`, not `partially_published`.

scheduledAt.description: When it is (or was) due to go out.

publishedAt.description: Set only once EVERY channel has published, so a non-null value is a reliable “this submission is completely done”. While channels are still resolving, each one’s own `publishedAt` is the authoritative answer.

channels.description: One entry per target account, in the order they were added.

tags.description: The workspace’s own labels for this submission — see `GET /public/v1/tags`. Empty when nothing is tagged. On the submission rather than on a channel, because that is what was tagged: one thing, filed under a word. Never published and never sent to a platform.

updatedAt.description: When any of its channels last changed.

PostBlock.description: One block of a chain — a tweet in a thread, a LinkedIn post or one of its comments.

media.description: Attachments on this block, in order.

items.description: One person tagged on an attachment, and where on it. Whether the coordinates are wanted is `limits.userTags.positioned` on GET /platforms — send both or neither.

username.description: The platform handle, without an `@`. A leading `@` and a pasted profile URL are stripped rather than refused. Nothing here checks that the account exists: a handle that resolves to nobody is published as a post that tags nobody, with no error anywhere.

x.description: Distance from the LEFT edge as a fraction of the width — 0.5 is the middle, whatever the picture was uploaded at. Not pixels: a fraction is what survives the platform re-encoding the file.

y.description: Distance from the TOP edge as a fraction of the height.

mediaUserTags.description: Who this block tags on each attachment, keyed by the media id they are tagged on, holding only the attachments that tag somebody. A map beside `media` rather than a field on each attachment, which is where this differs from `altText`: a description belongs to the file and is resolved onto it, while a tag belongs to this post on this platform. It comes back the way it was sent, so a post read here can be resubmitted verbatim.

remoteUrl.description: Where this block landed. Per block rather than only on the channel, because a five-tweet thread is five URLs. Null until it publishes.

PostChannel.description: One channel’s copy of a submission: its own status and result.

channelId.description: The connected account this went to. Null when that account has since been disconnected — the publication and its result survive, the link to a live channel does not.

platform.description: Null for the same reason `channelId` can be.

title.description: The post’s title, on platforms whose `limits.title` says they have that field. Null everywhere else.
title.example: How we cut our build time in half

postType.description: Which kind of thing this channel published — one of the `key`s in that platform’s `postTypes` on `GET /public/v1/platforms`. Null on a platform that publishes a single kind, and null where the submission asked for the default; both read the same way, as the `limits` at the top of that platform.

options.description: What this channel was given for its platform’s own fields — the values sent as `channels[].options`. Always an object, empty where nothing was sent. A value is a string, or an array of them for a field whose `type` on `GET /public/v1/platforms` is `list`; which one a key holds follows that declaration and never varies for a given key.

status.description: This channel’s own status, independent of its siblings.

error.description: Why this channel failed, in prose. Null unless `status` is `failed`.

remoteUrl.description: Where the first block landed. Null until it publishes.

blocks.description: The chain published to this channel. Always at least one entry.

PostMetricReading.description: One sample of one channel’s engagement. Shared `capturedAt` across every publication swept together, which is what makes two channels’ curves comparable at a point rather than merely adjacent.

capturedAt.description: When the sweep took this reading.

values.description:
The platform’s RUNNING counts at that instant, keyed by metric name.

AN ABSENT KEY IS NOT A ZERO — it was not reported at this capture, which on most platforms means it is never reported.

Cumulative since the post went out, so a curve only climbs. A value that DROPS between two readings is real and means people undid something.

PostMetrics.description:
One submission’s engagement CURVES, per channel — the series behind `GET /public/v1/stats`, which only ever sums the latest reading of each publication.

Cumulative and unevenly spaced: sampling decays from roughly hourly to weekly and stops at about thirty days, so plot against `capturedAt` and read an older post as frozen at its last reading rather than as having stopped earning.

postId.description: The submission these curves belong to.

metrics.description: Every metric name appearing anywhere in this response — the union of the per-channel lists, so one legend covers the whole submission. Empty when nothing has been reported for any channel. New names may be ADDED over time; treat an unrecognised one as a number you can display, not as an error.

channels.description: One entry per channel of the submission, in the same order as `channels` on `GET /public/v1/posts/{id}`.

PostMetricsChannel.description: One channel’s curve within the submission. Always present, even with no readings at all — omitting it would be indistinguishable from a channel the submission never went to, and "no readings" is the common case.

channelId.description: The connected account, an id from `GET /public/v1/channels` — and what to join on for that channel’s `metricsStatus`, which is where the reason for an empty curve lives. Null once the account has been disconnected: the readings survive, the link doesn’t.

platform.description: Platform id. Null for the same reason `channelId` can be.

metrics.description: Metric names appearing anywhere in THIS channel’s readings, in a stable order. A metric a platform started reporting partway through the post’s life is listed even though the earlier readings lack the key.

readings.description: Oldest first. Empty when nothing has been sampled for this channel — the normal case, not an error.

PostPage.description: A page of submissions, newest first.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `?cursor=` to fetch the next page. Null on the last page — that, not an empty `data`, is how a client knows to stop. Opaque by contract: do not parse it.

PostType.description: One kind of thing a platform publishes, with the limits that apply when you ask for it. The limits are complete rather than a diff — a kind of post is a different publication, not a variation on one.

key.description: Send this as `channels[].postType`. Stable; never displayed.

label.description: What the platform calls it. Display only.

help.description: One sentence about what choosing it means where the limits don't say it — that an Instagram Story disappears after 24 hours, for instance. Null where there is nothing to add.

channelId.description: Which channel’s copy of the submission the comment is on, an id from `GET /public/v1/channels`.

text.description: The reply. Held to the platform’s own limit, `limits.maxCharacters` on `GET /public/v1/platforms`.

RetractResult.description: What a retraction did, per channel. Two lists rather than a bare success, because the interesting outcome is partial: a submission spanning X and Instagram comes down on X and stays up on Instagram, and no HTTP status means both.

channelId.description: The channel, matching `channels[].channelId` on the submission. Null when the account has since been disconnected — the post outlives the connection, and there is then no token to reach it with.

platform.description: Its platform. Null for the same reason `channelId` is.

reason.description: Why this channel is in the list it is in, or null when the takedown succeeded. A sentence for a person to read — several of them are the platform's own words — so branch on which LIST the entry is in, never on this text.

removed.description: Channels whose copy is gone from the platform, and whose record went with it.

channelId.description: The channel, matching `channels[].channelId` on the submission. Null when the account has since been disconnected — the post outlives the connection, and there is then no token to reach it with.

platform.description: Its platform. Null for the same reason `channelId` is.

reason.description: Why this channel is in the list it is in, or null when the takedown succeeded. A sentence for a person to read — several of them are the platform's own words — so branch on which LIST the entry is in, never on this text.

remaining.description: Channels still live, each with a sentence saying why. A non-empty list means the submission still EXISTS, holding exactly these channels — so `GET /posts/{id}` keeps working and calling retract again takes down what is left.

content.description: The block’s new text. Optional and empty is fine — clearing the caption on a published image is a real edit. Send the block even when its text has not changed; unchanged blocks are not sent to the platform, so they cost nothing and never mark a post "edited".

RevisePostBlock.description: One block of the published chain. No attachments: no platform will change what a published post carries.

RevisePostChannel.description: One channel’s new wording. Every channel of the submission must appear — what you are describing is how the submission should now read, not a patch against it.

title.description: The title, on platforms that have one AND will change it after publishing — `limits.remoteEdit.fields` on `GET /public/v1/platforms` says which. YouTube will; Reddit will not, and sending one there is `edit_not_supported` rather than a field quietly ignored.

options.description: The platform’s own fields, where `limits.remoteEdit.fields` includes `options`.

blocks.description: Every block of the thread, in order, including unchanged ones. The length must equal what was published — adding or removing a block is `revision_structure_changed`.

RevisePostRequest.description: A revision: the submission as it should now read. Wording only — the channel list and each thread’s length must match what was published, and there is no field for attachments because no platform will change them.

channels.description: Every channel of the submission. Omitting one is `revision_structure_changed`, not a channel left alone — call `GET /posts/{id}` and edit what it returns.

ReviseResult.description: What a revision did, per channel. A refusal the API could see coming — a platform that edits nothing, a field outside its `remoteEdit.fields`, a structural change — is an ERROR instead, because nothing was sent.

channelId.description: The channel, matching `channels[].channelId` on the submission. Null when the account has since been disconnected — the post outlives the connection, and there is then no token to reach it with.

platform.description: Its platform. Null for the same reason `channelId` is.

reason.description: Why this channel is in the list it is in, or null when the rewrite succeeded. A sentence for a person to read — several of them are the platform's own words — so branch on which LIST the entry is in, never on this text.

revised.description: Channels whose live copy now reads as you sent it.

channelId.description: The channel, matching `channels[].channelId` on the submission. Null when the account has since been disconnected — the post outlives the connection, and there is then no token to reach it with.

platform.description: Its platform. Null for the same reason `channelId` is.

reason.description: Why this channel is in the list it is in, or null when the rewrite succeeded. A sentence for a person to read — several of them are the platform's own words — so branch on which LIST the entry is in, never on this text.

unchanged.description: Channels that were not rewritten. `reason` tells the two cases apart: null means there was nothing to send — the text already matched — and a sentence means the platform refused. They share a list because the common case is a submission where one channel was fixed and the rest were left alone, which is not a partial failure.

partNumbers.description: Which parts to sign, 1-based. Up to 100 per call.

mimeType.description: `video/mp4` or `video/quicktime`. Only video goes through upload sessions; every other kind is small enough for `POST /media`.

size.description: The file’s exact size in bytes. Checked against the plan’s video cap and storage allowance now, and against what actually arrived on complete.

Stats.description: Publishing ANALYTICS, not billing. Counted from the posts themselves, so deleting a post changes the history and these figures can go down. `GET /public/v1/usage` is the meter an invoice is computed from, and the only endpoint that predicts a 402.

from.description: Inclusive start of the window, as the server applied it.

timezone.description: The IANA zone `daily[].date` was bucketed in — the one requested, or `UTC`. Echoed because a day boundary is the whole meaning of a daily series: the same publication falls on different dates in different zones.

metrics.description: Metric names appearing anywhere in this response, in a stable render order. Empty when nothing was measured — which is how you tell "no engagement reported" from "this API has no engagement". New names may be ADDED over time; treat an unrecognised one as a number you can display, not as an error.

daily.description: One entry per day in the window, zero-filled and ascending.

channels.description: Busiest first. Every channel connected right now appears, including those that published nothing — a silent account is a finding, not an absence.

tags.description: Busiest first, and only tags something landed under — unlike `channels`, an unused label is omitted. These figures OVERLAP and do not partition `totals`: a publication carrying two tags is counted under both, one carrying none under neither. Do not render them as shares of a whole.

StatsChannel.description: One connected account's share of the window.

channelId.description: The connected account, an id from `GET /public/v1/channels`. Null on the single row collecting publications whose account has since been disconnected — which is what keeps these figures summing to `totals`.

platform.description: Platform id. Null for the same reason `channelId` can be.

StatsDay.description:
One calendar day of the window.

`engagement` here is what the posts published ON THIS DAY have earned, counted since each went out and still moving — NOT engagement earned on this day. The two are easy to confuse into a chart that is wrong in a way nobody can see; the second is not derivable from cumulative readings and this API does not offer it.

Days PARTITION the window, so unlike `tags` these do sum to the response-level `engagement`.

date.description: A CALENDAR DATE in `timezone`, not an instant. Parsing it as a timestamp re-reads it as UTC midnight and shifts the label a day in half the world.

StatsEngagement.description: What one bucket's publications EARNED, read back from the platforms.

values.description:
Summed cumulative counts keyed by metric name — the names listed in `metrics` on the response.

AN ABSENT KEY IS NOT A ZERO. It means no publication in this bucket reported that metric: either its platform does not measure it, or the platform reports no engagement to this API at all. Rendering a missing key as `0` states a fact about engagement that nothing measured.

Every value is the LATEST reading of each publication, summed — cumulative since the post went out, not earned during the window.

measured.description: Publications in this bucket carrying any reading at all — the denominator. Compare it against the bucket’s `published` before presenting any figure in `values` as a fact about the whole bucket.

StatsEngagementTotals.description: Engagement for the whole window, with per-metric coverage. Summed across CHANNELS, which partition the window — never across tags, which overlap.

values.description:
Summed cumulative counts keyed by metric name — the names listed in `metrics` on the response.

AN ABSENT KEY IS NOT A ZERO. It means no publication in this bucket reported that metric: either its platform does not measure it, or the platform reports no engagement to this API at all. Rendering a missing key as `0` states a fact about engagement that nothing measured.

Every value is the LATEST reading of each publication, summed — cumulative since the post went out, not earned during the window.

reported.description: How many publications reported each metric, keyed like `values`. What turns a total into a statement: 412 likes, from 31 of 44 publications.

measured.description: Publications in the window carrying any reading at all. Compare against `totals.published`.

StatsInsights.description: The window’s scored posts, grouped six ways. Every list is computed from the same posts, so groups within one list are comparable with each other.

from.description: Inclusive start of the window, as the server applied it.

timezone.description: The IANA zone weekdays and hours were read in.

compared.description: Posts that could be scored: published in the window, reporting engagement, on a channel with at least 3 such posts. Zero is normal on a workspace whose platforms report no engagement.

weekdays.description: Monday first. A day nobody posted on is ABSENT, not zero: no posts is no evidence.

hours.description: Midnight first. Absent when nobody posted then.

slots.description: Weekday and hour together, ordered by weekday then hour. Sparse: at most 168 entries, usually far fewer. Thin cells are common here; group neighbouring hours before naming a best time.

tags.description: Busiest first. OVERLAPPING: a post with two tags is in both, and an untagged post in none.

StatsQueue.description: A snapshot of RIGHT NOW. Unaffected by `from`/`to` — mixing pending work into a window total would produce a number meaning two things at once.

scheduled.description: Publications scheduled ahead of now, including any mid-flight.

drafts.description: Drafts held in the workspace, at any age.

StatsTag.description: One tag's share of the window. Overlapping rather than a partition — see the field description on Stats.

failed.description: Publications that were DUE in this window and errored. Placed by the time they were scheduled for, since a failure never got a publish time.

Tag.description: A workspace’s own label for a submission. Ours, not any platform’s: a tag is not a hashtag, is never published, and no provider is told it exists.

id.description: Use this in `tagIds` when creating a submission, and as `?tag=` when listing them. Address tags by id, never by name — the name is the field a workspace edits.

name.description: As the workspace typed it. Unique within the workspace, ignoring case.

color.description: A `#rrggbb` colour, for display only. Nothing filters or bills on it.

postCount.description: How many submissions carry it. Submissions, not rows: a tag on a post that went to four channels counts once.

UpdateWebhookRequest.description: Only the fields you send are changed — a partial update, despite the PUT. An endpoint has no parts to reconcile, so there is no half-state a partial body could leave behind.

enabled.description: Pause or resume delivery, keeping the id and the signing secret. Re-enabling also clears the failure streak, so a fixed receiver is not one flake from being switched off again.

file.description: JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, MP4, MOV, PDF, VTT or SRT. Images up to 10 MB, video and PDFs up to 100 MB, subtitle files up to 5 MB. A larger video, up to the plan’s video cap, goes through `POST /media/uploads` instead. Not every platform publishes every type — check `acceptedMimeTypes` on `GET /platforms`, where a PDF appears only for the platforms that publish a document post, and where a subtitle file appears on none: it is never an attachment, and reaches a platform through a `media` option instead (see YouTube’s `captionFile`). The bytes are proxied through the API rather than handed a presigned bucket URL, so the server sees the real content and a file whose bytes disagree with its declared type is rejected. A subtitle file sent as `application/octet-stream` — which is what an unconfigured client sends, since no system registers a type for `.srt` — is read from the filename’s extension instead, and then verified like everything else.

Usage.description: Consumption against the plan, for the whole ACCOUNT this workspace belongs to — a plan is bought once and every workspace its owner owns draws from one pool. These are the same events an invoice is computed from; a usage endpoint that disagreed with the bill would be worse than none.

plan.description: The tier the account behind this workspace is on.

periodStart.description: Inclusive start of the current billing period.

periodEnd.description: EXCLUSIVE end — the instant the period figures reset.

posts.description: Two figures because they answer different questions. `created` is what the monthly allowance is enforced against — the number that will refuse your next write. `published` is what a bill is computed from.

published.description: The billable figure: publications that actually reached a platform. Shares `created`’s limit; the allowance is one.

UsageMetric.description: One metered resource: what has been used, and the ceiling.

limit.description: Null means unlimited — not "unknown", and not a large number.

reason.description: What we found out. Only a human going back through OAuth in a browser fixes any of them, which is why this event exists.
reason.example: X refused to renew this account’s access. Reconnect it to publish again.

WebhookDelivery.description: One event’s journey to one endpoint, across every attempt made at it.

eventId.description: The event. Stable across every redelivery — this is what a subscriber dedupes on, and it is also the `id` in the body and the `X-Bulkit-Event-Id` header.

endpointId.description: The endpoint it was sent to.

status.description: `pending` — not accepted yet, and may still be retried. `succeeded` — your server returned a 2xx. `failed` — the retry budget is spent and nothing further will be attempted.

attempts.description: How many times we have sent it.

responseStatus.description: Your server’s HTTP status on the last attempt. Null when we never got one — DNS, TLS, refused, timed out. Your response BODY is never stored or returned.

error.description: Why the last attempt failed, in OUR words — never anything your server sent back.

durationMs.description: How long the last attempt took.

createdAt.description: When the event was queued for this endpoint.

WebhookDeliveryPage.description: A page of delivery attempts, newest first.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `?cursor=` for the next page. Null on the last page. Opaque by contract: do not parse it.

WebhookEndpoint.description: A registered destination for events. The signing secret is deliberately absent — it is returned only when the endpoint is created or its secret is rolled, and no route reads it back.

description.description: Your own label. Nothing else tells two endpoints apart.

events.description: What this endpoint receives. Never empty.

status.description: `disabled` means nothing is being delivered — either you switched it off, or we did after repeated failures. `disabledReason` tells them apart.

disabledReason.description: Why WE stopped delivering. Null while enabled, and null when you disabled it yourself — that needs no explanation from us.

secretLast4.description: Last 4 characters of the signing secret currently in force — enough to tell which secret a receiver is configured with, after the one time it was shown.

WebhookEvent.description: The body POSTed to your endpoint. Documented here for reference — no operation on this API returns it.

id.description: The event id, stable across every redelivery. Dedupe on this: delivery is at-least-once, so a receiver that 200s after its own timeout will be sent the same event again.

createdAt.description: When the fact became true — not when this attempt was sent.

WebhookPostData.description: The `data` of a `post.*` event. The whole submission travels with it, in the shape `GET /posts/{id}` returns, so an ordinary subscriber never has to call back.

channelId.description: The channel this event is about. `post.*` events fire ONCE PER CHANNEL — each channel of a submission publishes independently, with its own status and its own retry, so there is no single moment at which "the submission" published.

blocksPublished.description: How many blocks of the thread are live on the platform. On `post.partially_failed` this is less than `blocksTotal`, and the gap is the point: retrying resumes at the first unpublished block rather than re-posting the chain.

blocksTotal.description: How long the thread is. 1 for an ordinary post.

WebhookTestResult.description: How the test went. A failed test is still a 200: the request worked and the receiver did not, and `error` says why.

ok.description: True when your receiver answered with a 2xx.

responseStatus.description: Your receiver’s own HTTP status, or null when it never answered. Its body is never read back, for the reason given on the deliveries route.

error.description: Why it failed, in our words. Null on success.

durationMs.description: How long the attempt took, in milliseconds.
